projectDescription: Execution-time authorization infrastructure that evaluates, permits, and audits consequential actions — production deploys, financial transactions, AI agent tool calls, and regulated data operations — before they execute.
keyFeatures: Execution-time authorization gate: evaluate → permit → verify → execute → audit
Single-use permit tokens that enforce non-bypassable execution binding
Hash-linked, Ed25519-signed tamper-evident audit chain for compliance evidence
Policy-as-code with RACI rules, bundles, and GitOps sync
Human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval workflows with quorum support
GitHub Actions deploy gate for production.deploy protection
MCP server integration for LLM agent tool-call governance
LangChain and LlamaIndex middleware for AI agent authorization
Compliance framework support: 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, ICH E6, SOC 2
Vendor Qualification Package (VQP) generation for regulated industries
Fail-closed by default: network errors and timeouts block execution
Offline audit bundle verification with standalone CLI
publicApiSurface: POST /v1/evaluate — evaluate whether an action is permitted
POST /v1/verify-permit — consume a single-use permit token before execution
POST /v1/audit/exports — generate a signed, portable audit bundle
GET /v1/audit/events — list tamper-evident audit log entries
GET /v1/permits/{id} — retrieve a permit token by ID
POST /v1/decisions/{id}/replay — replay a past decision for forensic verification
POST /v1/policies — create or update a policy bundle
POST /v1/escalations — create a HITL approval request
POST /v1/webhooks — create an enforcement webhook subscription
SDK: protect() / withPermit() / with_permit() — fail-closed execution gate
SDK: evaluate() — raw decision with full response envelope
SDK: requirePermit() / require_permit() — explicit permit consumption
SDK: AtlaSentClient / AsyncClient — Python and TypeScript client constructors
CLI: atlasent-policy validate / test / diff / deploy
CLI: atlasent-audit-verify — offline audit chain verification
